transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been doing some weird things lately. At work and school. Like arranging receipts across the floor, or tapping the calculator in sets of nine. Sometimes I just stand by the copier with my hands up, and people ask if I’m okay. It’s… not really making sense.
Do you feel like you have to do these things, like arranging receipts or tapping the calculator?

Yeah… sort of. I don’t really know why I do it. I’ll just start lining the receipts up, or tapping the calculator like… nine times, and it feels hard to stop until it’s done. Same with standing by the copier with my hands up. It doesn’t make much sense.
Do you feel anxious if you can't arrange the receipts or tap the calculator the way you want to?
I… don’t know if I’d call it anxious. It just feels off if I stop, I guess. Like I need to finish it, but I haven’t really thought about it much.
Do you have any recurring thoughts that keep coming into your mind?
I’m not sure. I mean… not really thoughts, exactly. It’s more like I just end up doing the thing, and then I notice I’m doing it.
Do you feel like these actions, such as arranging receipts or tapping the calculator, are something you must do in response to a thought or a feeling?

I don’t think it’s really because of a thought. It’s more like… I just start doing it. Like the receipts, or tapping in nines, or standing there by the copier with my hands up. It doesn’t make sense to me either.
Do you feel distressed when you're doing these things, like arranging receipts or tapping the calculator?

Not exactly distressed while I’m doing it. More like… afterward I realize it looks strange. Like the receipts on the floor, or tapping the calculator that way. If someone notices, then I feel uncomfortable.
Do you feel like something bad would happen if you didn't complete one of these routines, like arranging the receipts or tapping the calculator?

No… I don’t think it’s like that. I don’t think something bad will happen. I just kind of end up doing it, like lining the receipts up or tapping the calculator that way, and then later I realize it didn’t really make sense.
Do you think doing these things, like arranging receipts or tapping the calculator, helps you feel better in any way?
Not really. I don’t think it helps me feel better. It’s just… I find myself doing it, like with the receipts or the calculator, and then I notice it doesn’t make much sense.
Do you find yourself doing these kinds of things at home as well?
A little, yeah. Mostly it’s been at work or school, though… like with the receipts, or the calculator. At home I don’t notice it as much.
What happens if someone or something stops you from finishing one of these routines, like arranging the receipts or tapping the calculator?

I usually just stop if they say something. It’s kind of embarrassing. Like if someone asks if I’m okay, I’ll realize I’m standing there with my hands up by the copier or doing the calculator thing, and I just… try to act normal again.
Do you feel like the things you arrange, like the receipts, need to be in a specific order or pattern?
Not really a specific order, I don’t think. It’s more like I just start lining them up, like across the floor, and then I realize it looks weird. I don’t know why I’m doing it.
Do you feel like you are trying to achieve a certain goal or prevent something unwanted when you do these repetitive actions?

No… I don’t think I’m trying to stop anything from happening. It’s not like that. I just kind of start doing it—lining receipts up, tapping the calculator a certain way, or standing there by the copier—and then I realize it doesn’t really make sense.
How do you feel if someone interrupts you while you're in the middle of one of these routines, like arranging receipts or tapping the calculator?

I guess I feel… embarrassed mostly. If someone interrupts me, I kind of snap out of it and notice I’m doing something weird, like the receipts or the calculator thing. I usually just stop and try to act like nothing happened.
Do you feel like you are doing these things, like arranging receipts or tapping the calculator, in response to an urge or impulse that you can't ignore?

I don’t know if it feels like an urge exactly. It’s more like I just… find myself doing it. Like the tapping in nines or standing by the copier with my hands up. I don’t really decide to, but I don’t know that I’m trying to ignore something either.
Do you feel like these actions are something you have to do, even if you don't want to?

Not really “have to,” I guess. I don’t feel like something bad will happen if I don’t. It’s more like I just catch myself doing it… lining stuff up or tapping the calculator, and then it feels stupid when I notice.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind that you can't get rid of?
Not really. I mean, I get stuck thinking about stuff sometimes, but I don’t think it’s like… thoughts I can’t get rid of. Not that I’ve noticed.
Do you feel anxious when you are stopped from finishing one of your routines, like arranging receipts or tapping the calculator?
I don’t think I get anxious, no. Maybe a little irritated if someone points it out, but not like… panic or anything. I usually just stop.
Do you feel like these actions are aimed at preventing something from happening?
No… I don’t think I’m trying to stop anything. It’s just weird stuff I end up doing, like lining receipts up or tapping the calculator a certain way. I don’t really have a reason for it.
